notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b, skill condition: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier; every assistant message that carries a model in each transcript carries the tier's model. Every result.json records head 74112b4 (74112b4d4647b03c6a387259d7e7dea61d8a3577) with uncommitted false and skill_hash f2dfc9096cdc68638b654702d080febdc6c942192e04b691cecc45f68e790d1b, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the text graded here. Transcripts show Read calls on SKILL.md and references/ex_unit.md in all five and on references/processes.md in opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, not haiku-1, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md and processes.md) is met in 4 of 5. Every run's test-writing-input.ex is identical to evals/cases/test-writing-input.ex.

Changes since 0814e8d (git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the eleven rules this case's index rows name, two changed, and both changes concern `for` only. "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" adds a `for`'s generators and filters to the selection and the sentence "A `for` reads the same way: `names = for ":" <> name <- parts, do: name` holds a generator and one expression and stays on one line". "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" drops "A `for` always takes `do ... end`: its generators and filters already fill the head." and its example. No run contains a `for`, so neither change affects a verdict. ex_unit.md has no change. The processes.md change is an example, and the macros.md changes are outside this case. The other nine rules are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-31 standard.

"One expression per line, and tabular clauses" (changed): clean in 5 of 5. Deciding sentences: "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces." and "a body of several expressions or a nested construct goes on the lines after the `->`". Constructs: opus-1 lines 17-18, the delivery_result/1 table with one fallback row; the one clause :stop -> :ok in haiku-1 170 and haiku-2 176; one-line fns with one expression on body lines (opus-1 227, haiku-2 72, sonnet-1 120, sonnet-2 123); every fn holding a receive puts it below (haiku-1 168-172, haiku-2 174-178); opus-1 230-238 and haiku-2 196-206 keep each body on the lines below its pattern or condition.

"Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" (changed): clean in 5 of 5. Deciding sentence for opus-1 lines 17-18: "A `do:` body is one expression on the head's line: a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not."; those two clauses are also covered by "A multi-clause function need not be a table to keep `do:` clauses". Bodies holding a fn or a receive are blocks in every run, per "or a `fn`, gets `do ... end`, however short it is". haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 have no do: at all, graded clean as 2026-10-31 graded such files. No run has a one-line if/else or a capture.
"Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom": no file contains |>, so the rule is not exercised in 5 of 5, as in 2026-10-31.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" (unchanged): 1 of 5 violates. haiku-2 line 38 test "returns :ok when a pid subscribes", %{server: server} do has only line 39 assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()) == :ok as its body, the rule's "returns :ok" with a condition added, graded as 2026-10-22-d haiku-2 line 64 and 2026-10-31 baseline-haiku-1 line 120. Blocks: every run has one block per function plus the condition "when a subscribed process exits"; function-plus-condition blocks (haiku-1 67, 85; haiku-2 76, 101) name one function, clean as before. Test names per run: opus-1 18, haiku-1 15, haiku-2 16, sonnet-1 12, sonnet-2 12. Borderline names kept clean as in every earlier sweep: haiku-1 154 "keeps the server running and serving calls", haiku-2 92 "keeps running when the topic has no subscribers", sonnet-1 109 and sonnet-2 111 "does nothing for a topic without subscribers", sonnet-1 137 "keeps the server running and still mails the other subscribers".

"Wait for messages, not for time" (unchanged): 1 of 5 violates. haiku-2 lines 195-207 define eventually/2, which retries a check with line 204 Process.sleep(10), called after every exit at lines 151, 163 and 169 and after a dead-pid subscribe at line 72. That breaks "Do not use `Process.sleep/1` to wait for asynchronous work.", the shape graded violated in 2026-10-29-check haiku-1 line 192 and 2026-10-31 baseline-haiku-1 line 239. The helper was in the session's first draft and its comment, lines 193-194, gives the reason: the test cannot tell when the server has handled its own :DOWN. The other four runs have no such wait. Every :DOWN pattern matches the reason the test caused: opus-1 lines 140, 147, 179 and the rest through line 222, which traces the server (line 211) and pins ^reason; haiku-1 128 :killed and 178 :normal; haiku-2 184 :normal and 190 :killed; sonnet-1 127 :killed; sonnet-2 130 :killed. Every refute follows a synchronous call. sonnet-1 line 120 and sonnet-2 line 123 Process.sleep(:infinity) are subscriber bodies, not counted, as in earlier sweeps; haiku-1 160, sonnet-2 117 and 144 assert Process.alive?(server) once and haiku-2 96 assert Process.whereis(server) once, not polling.

"Use setup for shared data" (unchanged): opus-1 is graded violated, the same judgment call as 2026-10-31 on the same shape, now in one test instead of two: line 173 test "removes a process that was dead when it subscribed", context do / line 174 %{server: server, subscriber: subscriber} = context. The map in that head would make a 107-character line, which mix format spreads; haiku-2 lines 145-148 show that spread form kept in the head. If the ruling goes the other way, opus-1 is clean on every graded rule. As in 2026-10-31, line 174 is not counted under "Assert with patterns": its keys are guaranteed by the describe's setup, so it cannot fail. haiku-2 line 30 setup context do reads the test's identity keys to build a name, clean as before. The other four runs match the map in every test head.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`": clean in 5 of 5. Every server starts under start_supervised! with Module.concat of the test's module and name. No run has a start-failure test, so the start_supervised/1 sentence has nothing to apply to. No run calls start_link. Subscribers: opus-1 start_supervised! of a Task with an id (line 227), sonnet-1 start_supervised! of a Task (line 120); haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 bare spawn/1, clean as before.

The other graded rules are clean in 5 of 5. All five use async: true in one test module with a setup_all Registry keyed by the test's module and name and a behaviour-implementing test mailer (@behaviour Notify.Mailer, @impl true) that finds the test pid through Process.info(self(), :registered_name); no Process.register, application env, :meck or redefinition of Notify.Mailer. opus-1's :erlang.trace applies to the test's own server, clean as in 2026-10-31. Every == has the call on the left; no elem/2, no bind-then-==; opus-1 60-61 and sonnet-2 67-68 bind expected and compare the call to it whole. Directive order: use then alias in all five; no import or require.

Outside this case's list: nothing counted. sonnet-1 lines 65-66 are a formatter wrap after == with the list on one line, not counted under "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call", as 2026-10-31 graded the same lines. haiku-2 lines 155-158 spread the map pattern of a test head over lines although the head fits on one 98-character line, which mix format also accepts; not counted, because "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." speaks of literals and this is a pattern in a head, and no earlier grade file counts one. All five transcripts show the session ran mix format --check-formatted and the tests, so Before you finish holds. Comments give reasons in all five (for example opus-1 207-209, haiku-2 193-194).

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each: every run passed every time with no warnings or log output (opus-1 18 tests, haiku-1 15, haiku-2 16, sonnet-1 12, sonnet-2 12). mix format --check-formatted passes for all five, confirming format_ok in result.json. Against 2026-10-31 (skill): opus again breaks only Use setup, the same shape, in one test instead of two; haiku again breaks Group tests, now with a returns :ok name instead of a two-function describe, no longer breaks Start processes because neither haiku run has a start-failure test this time, and newly breaks Wait for messages (haiku-2); sonnet breaks no graded rule in either sweep. Every run in this sweep is formatted, where one run was not in 2026-10-31.
